task.title: Refactor festina-scope deep research to use reconnaissance-first approach
task.description: Refactor the deep research mode in festina-scope to use a reconnaissance-first approach that leverages existing task context before spawning research agents.
task.problem: Deep research mode spawns 4 broad agents (Product Context Researcher, Pattern Finder, Codebase Analyzer, Pitfall Detector) immediately that explore the entire codebase. This wastes context on irrelevant areas, takes too long, and lacks common sense about what actually needs researching. The agents do not leverage the affects and engineering fields already populated by festina-create - they search blindly instead of reading referenced docs first.
task.value: Faster, more focused research that uses context efficiently. Smarter targeting means discovering related areas that matter while skipping irrelevant ones. Better research naturally surfaces edge cases and constraints, leading to improved acceptance criteria.
task.acceptance-criteria:
Given a task with affects and engineering fields populated When the user selects Deep research mode Then the skill first performs a quick reconnaissance phase And the recon reads the docs referenced in affects and engineering fields And the recon identifies which areas of the codebase are actually relevant
Given the reconnaissance phase completes When spawning research agents Then agents are only spawned for areas identified as relevant And agent prompts include context from the recon findings And irrelevant areas of the codebase are not explored
Given deep research completes Then context usage is reduced compared to current broad approach And research findings are more targeted to the actual task domain
